statements_method: Topics are the distinct claims each statement makes as recorded in 08 §4–5 from the statements read in the original; each distinct claim is one count, typed by what kind of evidence would settle it (09 §1). commons_2010.source: House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, HC 387-II (2009–10), The disclosure of climate data from the Climatic Research Unit at the University of East Anglia, Volume II: oral and written evidence — the 66 memoranda printed in it: the witnesses' submissions (CRU 00 and 00a–00d, 27, 48, 49, 49a, 53, 54) and the written evidence CRU 01–57 with the supplementary 25a, 26a and 37a. Read from the printed volume, publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200910/cmselect/cmsctech/387/387ii.pdf.
commons_2010.method: Two readings. (1) 2026-10-03: the 55 memoranda at the HTML addresses 387we02.htm–387we56.htm were each read by an automated summarizer (WebFetch) under a fixed instruction to list every distinct topic or allegation in one line, tag it DATA / PROXY / FOI / PEER / IPCC / MODEL / SENS / ATTR / SOLAR / INQ / OTHER, and state the submitter's stance; the GWPF's CRU 27 was added from the printed volume. (2) 2026-10-04: the full text of the printed volume was loaded in a browser and every memorandum read in full — the 55 by six delegated readers (Claude agents) under a fixed instruction to give each automated line a verdict (confirmed; retag, with the right tag; absent, where the memorandum does not make the point; duplicate), to add every distinct topic the lines missed at the same granularity, and to state the stance (critical: alleges misconduct by CRU or disputes the science; supportive; neutral: procedural or technical without taking a side; mixed) with a reason, a paragraph count, a verbatim characterising sentence and a one-sentence summary; the eleven witnesses' memoranda (CRU 00, 00a–d, 27, 48, 49, 49a, 53, 54) by the project itself under the same scheme. 'topics' holds the checked lines (absent and duplicate lines dropped, retagged lines carrying their new tag, added lines marked); 'topics_automated' the lines as the summarizer gave them. Tags map to the typology's types as before (DATA→D, PROXY→X, FOI/PEER/IPCC/INQ→PROC, MODEL→M, SENS→Q, ATTR and SOLAR→A), OTHER lines sorted into SOC, POL, FRAME, D, R, M or NOISE by hand for the lines added on reading and by keyword for the rest. 'Critical' in the tallies means stance critical or mixed. A topic line is one count; memoranda differ in length (2 to 56 paragraphs by the readers' counts), so the memorandum-level counts (how many memoranda raise a type at all) remain the safer measure.

topics.text: Peer review is the keystone of research integrity; UEA's codes require honesty, openness, accountability and integrity

The Russell review's terms address the three allegations (data manipulation, peer-review manipulation, FOI compliance) with discretion to extend them; a separate reappraisal of CRU's science with the Royal Society's help
The allegations, if proven, would damage CRU's contribution but, given the scale of international climate science, would hardly weaken its implications as a whole
Fabrication denied: CRU's primary station data come from national meteorological services or public collations such as GHCN, and its tree-ring data from collaborators or public databases

Station adjustments are standard homogenisation, applied to about 10 per cent of sites and documented in the 1985–86 technical reports; adjustments largely cancel in global averages; the Met Office's release of 80 per cent of CRUTEM3 stations reproduces the full record
The criticised computer programs were not used to produce CRUTEM3, and the CRUTEM3 program has been released by the Met Office

'Trick' and 'hide the decline' refer to the WMO 1999 diagram: the post-1960 divergence of one tree-ring series is a known phenomenon CRU itself published on; 'trick' meant a knack of presentation, not deception
Urbanisation in China (Jones et al. 1990): no concealment; the 2007 FOI request was answered; the 2008 reanalysis finds an urban effect of 0.1 °C per decade within a larger warming
CRU has not 'lost' primary station data, which exists in World Weather Records, NMS yearbooks and GHCN

Refusals to release NMS data reflect non-publication agreements; about 90 per cent of the stations are available from other sources; the July 2009 deluge of 61 requests; permissions sought from NMSs through the WMO and Met Office
Tree-ring measurements were not CRU's to release; embargoed by collaborators until their publications; released in 2008–09
The ICO's January 2010 statement was misreported: no breach of section 77 established, and the request concerned private e-mails, not raw data

The e-mail remarks about keeping McKitrick & Michaels 2004 and Soon & Baliunas 2003 out of AR4 preceded the AR4 planning meetings; both papers were cited in AR4; the doubts about their rigour were justified
The three global datasets share primary sources but are independent in adjustments and gridding; an unadjusted NCDC series and the reanalysis comparison (Simmons et al. 2010) agree with CRUTEM3
The Vice-Chancellor urges resistance to hearsay and 'orchestrated campaigns of misinformation' and encourages open debate
